observations: Long U-shaped/three-wing residence hall footprint around an open courtyard, consistent with the official GIS outline.
English Tudor brick exterior with extensive light limestone belt courses, window surrounds, and entrance portal.
Multiple steep slate roof planes with large front-facing gables/dormers, chimneys, and small roof openings; not a flat roof.
Several above-grade window rows plus low basement windows; exact total storeys and basement exposure remain uncertain.
The principal entrance is beneath a large gable/stone portal and a lion-and-shield feature above the doorway.
Facades have bay windows, grouped mullioned windows, and a regular repeated rhythm; exact measurements are unavailable.
method_and_limits: Direct inspection of the official 2004 exterior photograph and its Purdue archive metadata. The image establishes architectural vocabulary and broad roof/facade composition only; perspective and lack of georeferencing do not establish exact dimensions, roof plan, height, or entrance bearing.
